name: Question 5
problem: Let $T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]$ be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$
worked_solution:
The vector $v$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T)$ if there exists a vector $u=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]$ such that $T(u)=v.$

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot u & =v \\ [\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -5 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-3x+2y \\ -2y \\ -5x+y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3x+2y=5 \\ -2y=k \\ -5x+y=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $y=5x-1$, which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+2y & =5 \\ -3x+2(5x-1) & =5 \\ 7x & =7 \\ x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =5x-1 \\  & =5(1)-1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=4$ into the second equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2y & =k \\ -2(4) & =k \\ k & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $v\in \text{Im}(T)$ when $k=-8.$

Question 5
?

Let T=[−3200−20−510] be the standard matrix of the linear transformation T. Determine the value of k for which the vector v=[5k−1] belongs to Im(T).

a
−4
b
1
c
−1
d
−2
e
−8
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector v belongs to Im(T) if there exists a vector u=[xyz] such that T(u)=v.

Therefore, we must have

T⋅u=v[−3200−20−510][xyz]=[5k−1][−3x+2y−2y−5x+y]=[5k−1]

This gives the following system of equations:

{−3x+2y=5−2y=k−5x+y=−1.

From the third equation, we get y=5x−1, which we substitute into the first equation to get −3x+2y=5−3x+2(5x−1)=57x=7x=1.

Hence, y=5x−1=5(1)−1=4.

Finally, we substitute y=4 into the second equation and obtain

−2y=k−2(4)=kk=−8.

Therefore, v∈Im(T) when k=−8.
